 Alabama coach Nate Oats reflects on time with Antoine Pettway before matchup with Kennesaw State 
 The former Alabama assistant coach and player will return to Coleman Coliseum on Tuesday night as the head coach of Kennesaw State.
 Olivia Sayer 0 
 When Kennesaw State guard Davin Cosby Jr. found himself in a car accident two summers ago, head coach Antoine Pettway consistently stood by his side. 
 It didn't matter that Cosby, a former Alabama   and   Wake Forest transfer, could possibly never play the sport again. It didn't even matter that he might never suit up for the Owls.
 Pettway was there because he cared about his player.
 And that's what Alabama coach Nate Oats loved about him.
 "I just think Antoine cares about people," Oats said Monday. "And I think that's helped him become a great coach." 
 On Tuesday night, Alabama will welcome Pettway — a former player and assistant coach for the Crimson Tide — back to Coleman Coliseum, hosting Kennesaw State at 6:30 p.m. CT. Pettway spent four years on Oats' staff before earning the head coaching role. 
 He spent a total of 20 seasons with the Crimson Tide, including 15 as an assistant coach, four as a player and one as a graduate assistant.
 "I learned something from each one of those guys," Pettway said earlier this week. "I was blessed enough to be under some really really high-character, really really big-time coaches when I was there."
 SECOND CHANCE: How last 8 months changed Aden Holloway for better 
 (Photo: 247Sports)  
 Pettway wouldn't have found success without his extensive knowledge of the sport, but that's not what stood out to Oats when he looked back on his tenure. Instead, the head coach remembered the way Pettway interacted with his players.
 He recalled the way he kept the Alabama roster together after Oats was hired, leaning on his relationships to retain athletes like Kira Lewis Jr. , Herbert Jones , John Petty Jr. , Alex Reese and Javian Davis through the transition.
 It's why Oats was thrilled to keep him on the staff — after conducting interviews, where it was apparent that Pettway recruited most of the team — upon accepting the position in March 2019. 
 "He was elite at the relationships," Oats said. "Managing situations, managing players. His level of care for the player as an individual, as a young man, was always as good as anybody I've ever worked with." 
 Pettway brought those qualities to Kennesaw State, where he's since flourished. After taking two seasons to establish the foundation, he led the Owls to the NCAA Tournament last year, their second-ever appearance. Kennesaw State won the Conference USA tournament to earn the bid.
 A TEAM EFFORT: Alabama plays 'unselfish' in victory over Oakland 
 This year, the Owls are off to another solid start, entering Tuesday's contest 4-0 with victories over Midway, Austin Peay , Winthrop and LaGrange. Kennesaw State averages over 95 points per game while allowing less than 65 per matchup. 
 But as impressive as Pettway's team is on the court, it was his devotion to his players that Oats will always remember him for. 
 "He does a lot of other things really well, but I think that's what kind of separates him from some of the other (coaches)," Oats said. "Hopefully our fans welcome him back."
